title: Backflow preventer rebuild: when a kit is plausible?봞nd when it is not
description: Use the model, size, failure location, and service history to decide whether to request a rebuild quote, a repair visit, or a replacement comparison.
prompt: Should this backflow preventer be rebuilt?
answer: A rebuild is a model- and size-specific repair path, not a universal kit purchase. Confirm the exact assembly, approved parts availability, body condition, and required retest before comparing rebuild and replacement.
urgency: Treat active discharge, freezing damage, corrosion, missing parts, or a failed containment test as a reason to have a qualified technician assess the assembly. Do not open a pressurized device or buy parts from a photo alone.
diagramAlt: Reduced-pressure backflow assembly with serviceable check and relief zones

choices.label: The device failed a test

choices.label: The body is damaged or old

steps.title: Identify the site condition
steps.body: Record manufacturer, model, nominal size, serial number if present, and a full-device photo.

steps.title: Define the complete scope
steps.body: Identify the failure location from a certified test report or qualified service diagnosis.

steps.title: Close the compliance loop
steps.body: Verify that an approved kit exists for that exact model and size and that the device body is serviceable.
Compare a rebuild quote with replacement scope, including isolation, piping changes, retest, and required report filing.
